# A sharp surviving invariant for common continuous Minkowski addition

Let n>=0,d>=1, and let C be a compact convex body with at least one nonempty
integer fiber. Let L be a d-dimensional convex body, of volume ell>0 and
centroid g_L. Put

    C_t=C+({0}x tL), S_t=C_t intersect (Z^n x R^d), t>=0,
    mu_t(A)=sum_z |K_z(t) intersect A_z|,
    D_t(y)=inf{mu_t(H): H closed ambient halfspace, y in H},
    D_*(t)=sup_(y in S_t) D_t(y).

All measures here are mixed d-volume, even when mu_0 happens to vanish;
for positive t every nonempty fiber has positive d-volume. This note is
not an intrinsic-measure replacement at t=0 when q<d.

For every s,t>=0 and every y in S_t,

 D_(t+s)(y+(0,s g_L))^(1/d)
    >=D_t(y)^(1/d)+s gamma_d^(1/d)ell^(1/d).         (1)

Consequently

 D_*(t+s)^(1/d)
    >=D_*(t)^(1/d)+s gamma_d^(1/d)ell^(1/d).         (2)

The added constant is sharp, including at n>=1. This is an unnormalized
growth statement; it does not imply quasiconcavity of normalized depth.

Proof. Convexity of L gives tL+sL=(t+s)L, and the actual integer fibers
satisfy K_z(t+s)=K_z(t)+sL. In particular the indicated shifted center
belongs to its original integer fiber of S_(t+s).

Let H contain this new center, and translate it by -(0,s g_L) to obtain a
parallel halfspace H' containing y. If u is the continuous part of its
normal and u!=0, let L^+=L cap {u.(x-g_L)>=0}. Its volume is at least
gamma_d ell by ordinary Grunbaum. For every old cap fiber A_z=K_z(t) cap H'_z,

    A_z+sL^+ subset K_z(t+s) cap H_z.               (3)

This follows by adding the affine margins: the new margin of a+sv equals
the old margin of a plus s u.(v-g_L). Thus (3) includes all oblique integer
coefficients, and no cap-orientation assumption is introduced. When u=0,
use L^+=L instead; all included old fibers stay included, and its volume
ell is at least gamma_d ell.

Put c=s gamma_d^(1/d)ell^(1/d), and let f_z=|A_z|. If
F=sum f_z>0, Brunn--Minkowski in every positive-volume old cap fiber gives

    mu_(t+s)(H)>=sum_(f_z>0)(f_z^(1/d)+c)^d
                  >=(F^(1/d)+c)^d.                (4)

For the last inequality expand the integer power. For each exponent
0<p<=1, sum f_z^p>=(sum f_z)^p, and the constant term is counted at least
once. These elementary inequalities prove (4) also when some old cap
fibers have zero volume; new contributions from them are nonnegative.
As F>=D_t(y), (4) gives the desired lower bound for this H.

If F=0, then D_t(y)=0. The set y+(0,sL^+) is contained in the new cap and
in the selected actual fiber, so that cap has mass at least c^d. This is
the same lower bound. For s=0 the assertion is tautological. Taking the
infimum over all H proves (1), including vertical closed boundary mass.

Taking the supremum over old points proves (2). No maximizer is needed
for this step: apply (1) along any sequence approaching the old supremum,
which is finite by compactness and finitely many integer fibers.

For sharpness, take L to be a d-simplex, epsilon>0, and
C=[0,1]^n x epsilon L (or just epsilon L if n=0). Then S_t has 2^n identical
simplex fibers (epsilon+t)L. The ordinary centroid in any one fiber has
unnormalized depth at least gamma_d(epsilon+t)^d ell from that fiber.
Conversely each integer vertex can be isolated with a sufficiently large
integer tilt, and every point in its simplex has an own-fiber cap of mass
at most gamma_d(epsilon+t)^d ell. Hence

    D_*(t)=gamma_d(epsilon+t)^d ell,

and (2) is an equality. The isolation argument is unnecessary when n=0.

The explicit normalized-depth dip in
`candidate 121d9e12ac57cde9` remains valid: the
total mixed volume also grows, and (2) places no matching restriction on
that denominator. Even the root of unnormalized depth need not be concave
in t; the interval example has increasing piecewise-linear slopes two and
three. The proved invariant is the lower growth (1)--(2), precisely as stated.
